Why we ask you to transfer money

The payment acts as a security check.

Your current bank has already confirmed your identity. When you send us money from an account in your name, we can use that existing verification to confirm it’s really you. We need this step to follow banking laws.

The money is yours to use right away once your account is ready.

What information do we see?

We only check the details we need to confirm the money came from an account in your name:

The name on the bank account

The IBAN or account number

We won’t see your bank statements or activity, and we can’t take money out of your account.

If the confirmation fails, we will pay your money back automatically by the end of the day.

Submit your residence permit within 6 months

To comply with German regulations, we need to collect your valid residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel).

About eID

eID is a secure digital feature built into your official identity card that lets you prove your identity online.

How to check if you have eID

  • Look for the logo: Check if the back of your card has the green and blue circle symbol.
  • Check the issue date: German ID cards (Personalausweis) issued after July 2017 have eID activated by default.

    Issued between Nov 2010 – June 2017? Your eID may be disabled, but you can activate it anytime at your local Bürgeramt.

About eID PIN

The 5-digit PIN from your government letter is a one-time setup code used to create your secret 6-digit personal PIN.

How to check if you have eID

  • In your mail: When your ID was issued, you received a government letter (PIN-Brief) containing a 5-digit Transport PIN.
  • Forgotten PIN? If you set a 6-digit PIN and forgot it, or lost your letter, you can get a new PIN set at any local Bürgeramt or Ausländerbehörde.

Which countries are in the EEA?

EAA includes all EU countries, plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.
